chunks: And a group informed me, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: Narrated to us Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj the Mu'adhdhin, who said: Narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Karkhi, who said: I heard Abu Harun - a man from our companions - saying: I saw the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), and his face shone like the moon on the night of the full moon, and I saw hair on his navel running like a line, and he lifted the garment from him and found him circumcised, so I asked Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: Thus he was born, and thus we were born, but we passed the knife over him to adhere to the Sunnah.
ai.seo_question: Was the Imam of the Age circumcised and why?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological principle of *Iqtida’ al-Sunnah* (adhering to the Sunnah for consistency) rather than necessity, affirming that the Imams, though born in a state of natural purity (*fitrah*), undergo circumcision to align with the prophetic tradition. The detail of the hair on the navel (*shu’rat al-sirr*) serves as a distinctive physical sign (*‘alam*) of the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing their unique lineage and status. This hadith is central to Shia jurisprudence in resolving the debate between those who view the Imams' actions as purely ritualistic versus those who see them as indicative of legal rulings.
